keyTerms.definition: Fitted power law: loss linear in log-log space vs scale.
Instruction tokens carry zero weight.
W = W0 + (alpha/r)BA; 128x fewer trainable on the toy.
P(A beats B) = sigmoid(r_A - r_B).

recall.question: Write the two-point scaling-law fit and the compute budget formula C = 6ND.
recall.answer: b = (log10 L2 - log10 L1)/(log10 N2 - log10 N1), L(N) = 10^(a + b log10 N). C = 6ND: 2N forward + 4N backward per token.

recall.question: Write the masked SFT loss. Which tokens carry zero weight, and why?
recall.answer: Loss = -mean over response tokens of log P(y_t | x, y_<t). Instruction tokens carry zero weight so the model learns responses, not instructions.

recall.question: Write the LoRA update and its parameter count vs full fine-tuning.
recall.answer: W = W0 + (alpha/r)BA. Trainable: r(d+k) vs dk. Toy 4096/16: 131,072 vs 16,777,216 (128x).

keyTerms.definition: -0.0748 per decade on the toy fit.
Wins with exactly two runs and no visible floor.
Data mix changes break the N-only law.

recall.question: Fit the two-point law on N1=1e9 L1=2.40, N2=1e10 L2=2.02 and predict N=1e11.
The big run beats the prediction by 0.2. Name two causes.
recall.answer: Recipe changed (data mix/optimizer) between runs, or seed luck on the single big run.

keyTerms.definition: Scores responses from pairwise votes.
Penalizes distance from the SFT policy.
Reward up, human ratings down.
Fewer moving parts when preference data is fixed.

recall.question: RLHF toy: r_A=1.2, r_B=0.8, KL=2.5, beta=0.1. Compute P(A wins) and the objective.
Reward climbs, human ratings fall. Name the failure and the first fix.
recall.answer: Reward hacking. First fix: raise beta (tighten the leash) or audit the reward model.

keyTerms.definition: C = 6ND.
Under 1 std: none; 2.5 std: real.

recall.question: Scaling toy: C = 6ND with N=1e9, D=2e10. The budget doubles. What loss drop?
recall.answer: C = 1.2e20. Doubling buys 0.301 decades of N: loss falls ~5% relative.

recall.question: Seed sweep losses [2.31, 2.29, 2.33, 2.30, 2.32]. Recipe B reports 2.295, a third 2.27. Verdicts?
recall.answer: Mean 2.31, std 0.0158. B: gap < 1 std, no evidence. Third: gap 2.5 std, evidence of a real win.

keyTerms.definition: Per-bin mask blocking cross-document attention.
Every query attends only within its own document.

recall.question: The packing code fills bins but training diverges on long documents. Find the bug, fix it, state the invariant.
recall.answer: Bug: no document mask, attention leaks across packed documents. Fix: return (bins, masks). Invariant: every query attends only within its own document.

keyTerms.definition: RLHF dominates; RLAIF keeps a niche.
Packing, LoRA, scaling still matter.
Simplicity with a fixed preference set.

recall.question: Human labels are free and instant. Does RLAIF still have a role?
recall.answer: RLHF dominates on quality per label. RLAIF keeps a role only for rules humans cannot label consistently. DPO wins on simplicity with a fixed set.

recall.question: The cluster price drops to zero but the power cap stays. Which U06 levers still matter?
recall.answer: Packing (time-to-loss), LoRA (memory per task), scaling still matter. Cost-per-token and loader levers die.

keyTerms.definition: Same eval? Easier suite invalidates.
Threshold vs continuous: the jump may be measurement.

recall.question: A paper claims “our 1B model matches a 10B model, so scaling laws are broken.” List five audit questions.
recall.answer: (1) Same eval? (2) Same data? (3) Same metric? (4) Cherry-picked tasks? (5) One seed?
